title: Reverse an array
problemStatement: Reverse an array in-place (iterative two pointers and recursive).
intuition: Swap ends and move inward. Recursive version: swap a[l],a[r] then recurse l+1,r−1. Same O(n) swaps; iterative uses O(1) aux, recursive uses O(n) stack.

approaches.title: Optimal: two pointers (iterative)
Recursive two pointers
limitations: Prefer iterative in production / large n

specialTechnique.title: In-place O(1) extra space
specialTechnique.body: Two-pointer swap modifies the input array without allocating another array. Distinguish auxiliary space O(1) from input space O(n).

complexity.space: O(1) aux iterative; O(n) stack recursive

commonMistakes: Building a new reversed list when in-place was required
patternRecognition: Same pattern as palindrome check on arrays
interviewInsight: State “O(1) auxiliary, in-place” explicitly — interviewers listen for that phrase.
